notes: ACCESS: opened exclusively through the Claude-in-Chrome connector in my own tab (tabId 1961713834); no HTTP client, proxy or reader was used. robots.txt (https://www.thesocialitefamily.com/robots.txt) names no Claude/anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot agent at all - only a generic 'User-agent: *' block that disallows /api/* but explicitly Allows /api/*sitemap.xml$; collection pages are not disallowed, so extraction is permitted. TREE: taken from the site's own E-shop mega-menu (opened by clicking the 'E-shop' button on https://www.thesocialitefamily.com/en-eu/), which has five departments - FURNITURE, LIGHTING, DECORATIVE, TEXTILES, plus a DISCOVER promo column. The FURNITURE department contains exactly: Sofa, Chair and armchair, Barstool, Bench, Footstool, Coffee table, Dining table, Headboard, Bedside table, Storage and desk, Outdoor, View all. Cross-checked against the collections sitemap (https://www.thesocialitefamily.com/api/collections-sitemap.xml, 329 /en-eu/ collection handles) - the only other furniture-shaped handles there are SEO/filter landing pages (table-basse-marbre, canape-en-velours, canape-bouclette, pouf-carre, pouf-en-velours, banc-cannage, chaise-de-bar-metal, chaise-de-bureau-design, canape-modulable, table-basse-en-travertin, table-a-manger-en-marbre, table-a-manger-en-travertin, table-de-chevet-bois-1, mobilier-bois, chambre-denfant, edito-* editorial pages) which are material/colour/room filter re-cuts, not nav nodes, and are excluded per section 3. Every FURNITURE leaf's own on-page sub-nav links only to its siblings, so the furniture tree is exactly one level deep - no grouping rows below the 'Furniture' Category bucket. PLATFORM/QTY: headless Shopify on a Next.js frontend; listing pages are Algolia InstantSearch and render NO visible 'N products' header anywhere, so per section 4.2 the count comes from the server-embedded Algolia initialData in the RSC payload of each collection page (props...defaultQueryOptions.initialData.pages[0].nbHits), which is scoped by filters=collectionsHandles:"<handle>" to that exact collection. Validation done: (a) exhaustiveNbHits:true present for every collection read; (b) ceil(nbHits/24)==nbPages holds for all 11 leaves (hitsPerPage=24 site-wide); (c) <h1> of each fetched page matches the expected category name (guards against a parent listing being silently served); (d) LAST-PAGE REMAINDER ENUMERATION - on /collections/canape?page=10 the rendered grid holds exactly 5 product cards = 221-9*24, and on /collections/mobilier?page=17 exactly 9 = 393-16*24, proving nbHits is the true Algolia total and hitsPerPage really is 24; (e) two independent reads of all 11 leaves taken minutes apart returned identical numbers - no drift; (f) all 11 numbers differ from each other and from the parent, so this is not a site-wide constant. NOTE on the grid: intermediate pages show 20 product cards plus 2 'shop the look' selection cards; each selection card occupies 2 product slots (20+2*2=24), which is why a full page renders 20 products - verified on outdoor (10 product cards + 2 selection cards = 14 = nbHits) and on mobilier page 2 (20 + 2 = 22 grid children). EXCLUDED from the FURNITURE menu: 'View all' (=/collections/mobilier, nbHits 393) is the parent roll-up and is section-3 navigation junk, and its children overlap it (they sum to 466 > 393 because outdoor/in-stock items are cross-filed), so it is not emitted at all; 'Rotondo cover' (/collections/housse-rotondo, nbHits 65) is sofa slipcovers = furniture covers, a standing section-1 exclusion; 'In-stock furniture' (/collections/mobilier-en-livraison-rapide) is an availability filter; 'New collection' (/collections/la-vita-lenta), 'Archives' (/collections/dernieres-pieces), 'Selection of the week', 'Wild patterns' are seasonal/clearance/marketing collections. Nothing furniture-typed was found in the LIGHTING, DECORATIVE or TEXTILES departments (cushions, vases and planters, tableware, candles, small items, mirrors, rugs, book, table linen, throws, curtains, bed linen). OVERLAP: the 7 furniture items inside Outdoor are also carried in Sofa and Chair and armchair; both nodes are real, separately-named menu entries with their own scoped listing, so both are kept, per the brief's 'keep both and explain' rule.
